title: A nurse-led weight clinic versus usual advice for overweight dogs with osteoarthritis in first-opinion practice: a pragmatic trial
abstract: Objective: to compare a nurse-led weight clinic with usual vet-led advice on owner-reported mobility in overweight dogs with osteoarthritis. Design: pragmatic trial in 12 first-opinion practices with individual central allocation stratified by practice. Primary outcome: change in an 11-item owner-reported mobility index at six months. Results will be reported after follow-up.
introduction: Excess weight worsens osteoarthritis in dogs, and supervised weight loss improved mobility in a referral trial, but nurse-led clinics in first-opinion practice have not been compared with usual advice, and most dogs stop attending.
methods: Dogs with osteoarthritis and a body condition score of 7 or more were allocated 1:1 by a central web system. The primary analysis compares six-month index scores adjusted for baseline and practice by intention to treat; lameness was scored from video by vets unaware of allocation.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the CONSORT flow diagram, baseline characteristics, the adjusted difference in mobility, weight change, blinded lameness, attendance and hunger behaviours.
discussion: The discussion will compare owner-reported and blinded outcomes, weigh attendance against effect, and state what the result means for roll-out across the group.
limitations: Owners were not blinded; six-month follow-up; one practice group.
conclusion: To be written after the analysis; limited to the comparison in this practice group.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT with the pragmatic trials extension
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty until follow-up ends.
